title: Sensitive Output Manual Review Routing & Cost Allocation — Template
content:
Purpose:
This template annex defines an operational and contractual framework for routing inference outputs to human reviewers, the security and privacy controls reviewers must follow, and an auditable cost-allocation mechanism when manual review is performed by a vendor or third-party. It is intended to be attached to Vendor Agreements, DPA annexes, or Service Order schedules.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to any product/module where model outputs may be flagged for manual review (e.g., content moderation, sensitive PII detection, high-risk decisions).
- Covers triggers, routing rules, reviewer access, retention and pseudonymization requirements, reviewer SLAs, cost allocation/chargeback, and evidence/audit obligations.
- Does not alter broader data protection commitments in the main DPA; it is an operational exhibit that supplements the DPA.

Definitions (short):
- "Flag": an inference response marked (by model confidence, rule, or customer signal) for human review.
- "Reviewer": an individual (vendor employee or Redwood staff) who inspects flagged outputs.
- "Manual Review Event": single routing of an output to a reviewer and any subsequent reviewer actions.
- "Redaction/Pseudonymization": removal or replacement of sensitive identifiers prior to review where feasible.

Routing triggers (configurable):
- Confidence thresholds: e.g., model confidence < 0.15 OR > 0.95 for specific safety classes.
- Keyword/rule matches: presence of customer-sensitive tokens or regulated categories (health, finance, legal).
- Customer override: route if customer sets "force_review" flag in request metadata.
- Sampling policy: X% of outputs for model health sampling (default 1%); ensure sampling is uniformly random unless otherwise specified.

Routing rules and prioritization:
- Priority tiers: P0 (legal/regulated), P1 (safety/harm), P2 (quality), P3 (sampling).
- Failover: If primary reviewer pool unavailable, route to secondary pool in same region; if none available, follow automated fallback defined in main SLA (e.g., redact + return automated response).
- Regional controls: reviewers must be located only in allowed jurisdictions defined per customer profile (e.g., EEA-only review).

Reviewer access & security controls (must be contractually required of vendor):
- Least privilege access to the minimum data required to complete review.
- Ephemeral credentials for reviewer workstations with session timeouts <= 15 minutes of inactivity.
- MFA mandatory for all reviewer accounts.
- Prohibit data export; block clipboard screenshots and external storage during active review sessions where technically feasible.
- Mandatory CS/HR background checks and NDA attestation for reviewers assigned to regulated customer cohorts.

Data minimization & pseudonymization policy:
- Where possible, redact direct identifiers before routing (names, account IDs).
- Provide reviewers a pseudonymized context window; customer can opt into full-text review for troubleshooting with explicit consent.
- Retain original (unredacted) material only where legally required and store with heightened controls and access logging.

Retention & deletion:
- Manual Review Records (metadata only) retained for at most 12 months unless otherwise contractually extended.
- If any full outputs are stored for QA, they must be marked and retained no longer than 90 days by default.
- Deletion workflow: vendor must implement near-real-time deletion API and provide signed deletion receipts on request.

SLA & reviewer performance metrics (example):
- P0/P1 reviews: initial human response within 1 business hour, resolution within 6 business hours.
- P2 reviews: response within 4 business hours, resolution within 48 hours.
- Sampling/P3: batched review cadence (daily/weekly) as agreed.
- Accuracy/consistency: vendor provides quarterly reviewer concordance reports (sampled) with target >= 90% agreement against Redwood-defined adjudication set.

Cost allocation model (example clauses to include in contract):
- Unit of charge: per Manual Review Event (MRE). An MRE = single output presented to a reviewer for adjudication.
- Tiered pricing (sample): 0–10k MRE/month = $0.20/MRE; 10k–100k = $0.12/MRE; >100k = $0.08/MRE.
- Minimum monthly commitment: Parties may agree a minimum MRE commitment for capacity planning; unconsumed MREs may be credited month-to-month for up to 3 months.
- Overage and emergency review rates: higher per-MRE rate applies for after-hours or expedited P0 reviews; clearly define what constitutes after-hours.
- Cost transparency: vendor must provide daily MRE logs with timestamps, reviewer IDs, and routing reason codes to support customer billing reconciliation. Logs may be pseudonymized (reviewer ID pseudonym) but must be cross-referenceable via vendor-secure mapping when required for audit.

Auditability & evidence obligations:
- Vendor to furnish monthly attestation of compliance with the access and retention controls in this annex.
- On-request evidence: vendor must produce (within 10 business days) audit samples, reviewer training records, and deletion receipts for specific MREs.
- Penetration & process audits: mutually agreed external audits allowed annually; scoped to review operations and reviewer access controls; vendor to cover the costs of remediation.

Liability and indemnity (example language):
- For breaches caused by reviewer misconduct or vendor operational failure (unauthorized disclosure), vendor indemnifies customer for direct damages up to a defined cap (e.g., direct damages equal to fees paid in the prior 12 months), except where higher statutory liabilities apply.
- For misclassification errors leading to customer loss (e.g., incorrect suppression of lawful content), liability limited to actual direct damages; parties to discuss carve-outs for willful misconduct.

Termination & migration:
- Termination for cause: material breaches of reviewer access/no-export or failure to delete on request may trigger termination rights.
- Data handback: upon termination, vendor must provide an export of any retained full outputs or pseudonymization mapping within 30 days and then delete remaining copies; deletion certificates to be provided.

Operational playbook (appendix):
- Quick checklist for onboarding a new customer cohort: regional limits, required background checks, redaction policies, and billing tier selection.
- Sample routing codes (to standardize logs): RC-01: low-confidence; RC-02: PII-detected; RC-03: customer-forced; RC-04: model-fail-safe.
- Escalation ladder for disputed adjudications: reviewer -> senior reviewer -> Redwood safety team -> customer policy owner.

Implementation notes / technical guidance (working doc section):
- Recommend implementing review queues as immutable events with idempotent retry to avoid double billing.
- Use encryption at rest with separate KMS keys for flagged records.
- Prefer pseudonymization at ingestion to reduce surface area; keep mapping table in HSM-backed store with restricted access.
- Consider differential sampling for model drift detection vs. safety review to avoid mixing responsibilities in cost-center accounting.

Open questions for legal/pricing teams (to resolve before finalizing template):
- Acceptable liability cap tiers for SMB customers vs. enterprise?
- Default regional reviewer jurisdiction policy for "global" customers that did not specify preferences?
- Should Redwood or vendor provide reviewer training materials and how to evidence completion?

Change log / notes:
- 2025-11-20: Initial draft by Sofia Martinez (security).
- 2025-12-05: Added cost examples and retention windows (collab: Ethan Reed).
- 2026-01-18: Inserted SLA examples and audit turnaround times (Priya Nair).
- 2026-02-10: Reviewed for regional compliance flags and added migration clause (Daniel Park).

Annex placeholders (to be filled per customer):
- Agreed reviewer jurisdictions: __________
- MRE committed volume and baseline tier: __________
- Sampling fraction for model health: __________
- Escalation contact list: __________

Notes to negotiators (internal):
- Push for vendor to accept deletion receipt obligation with cryptographic signature to avoid disputes.
- Prefer unit pricing over hourly reviewer billing to keep incentives aligned with automation.
- For high-risk customers consider a pass-through premium for background-checked reviewer pools.

End of template.

(Working doc — intended for inclusion as an exhibit or schedule into Vendor Agreement / DPA. Treat as negotiable; keep track of redlines in linked artifacts.)
